summary: The shipped @zodiacs/engine 0.1.1-rc.6 position chain (chunk-GBH7JIYF.js) is physically sound in its reduction steps for planets (iterated light-time, first-order aberration, IAU 2006 precession, of-date true-obliquity rotation) but its accuracy is capped by the SERIES it evaluates, not by the reduction: astronomy-engine ships a VSOP87 truncated to 12-58 longitude terms per planet (Neptune 13 terms, smallest kept 18.6"), an Improved-Lunar-Ephemeris Moon, and a custom Pluto integrator. With the time scale pinned to TT, daily 2025 residuals against Swiss are Neptune +11.6" (max 12.2", lat 9.6"), Saturn -7.8", Uranus -1.4" (lat +4.1"), Jupiter -2.0", Venus/Mercury up to 5-7", Sun up to 1.4", Moon p50 0.68"/max 3.6"; the geometric-only comparison against DE440s reproduces the same numbers, and JPL Horizons (DE441) confirms the biases are the engine's (Saturn -8.33", Neptune +11.50" vs Horizons while Swiss sits at +0.05"). Swiss's own .se1 (DE431) agrees with DE440s to 0.003" over 2025, so 'moving to DE440' buys nothing against Swiss by itself; abandoning the truncated series is the whole gain. Three things matter most: (1) the series replacement (all bodies, incl. Moon and Pluto, which is 29" off at 2200 and 33" at 2400); (2) Delta-T: astronomy-engine's Espenak-Meeus polynomial is 6.7 s above Swiss and at least 5.4 s above any physically possible value today (TT-UTC = 69.184 s), displacing the 2026 Moon by 3.4" and growing to 110 s / 54" at 2100 and 280 s / 173" at 2200, and the package neither exposes nor documents Delta-T; (3) a frame inconsistency in the same chunk: computeChart hands the angles the MEAN obliquity while the bodies sit on the TRUE ecliptic of date and the sidereal time is apparent, which measured against Swiss houses_ex puts the Ascendant off by up to 18.5" at London and 13" at Longyearbyen today (the committed 1.57" polar pack understates this because it is six instants). Smaller but real: the true node carries a -7.25" mean bias (p50 7.0", max 19.9") that is provably a Moon-velocity error and not a definition difference (rebuilding the node from Swiss's own state reproduces Swiss to 1"); the Moon route omits light-time+aberration whose net is a constant -0.70"; nutation keeps 5 of 77 terms (0.2685" max 1900-2100, reproduced); solar deflection is absent (1.14" measured for Jupiter at 0.26 deg elongation); the +-6 h central-difference speed is off by up to 7.5"/day for the Moon but never flips a retrograde flag except inside a <=38 min window around stations that is itself set by the series, not the derivative. One task premise was false and is recorded: Swiss 2.10.03 cannot read the NAIF de440s.bsp (retflag 260 = MOSEPH fallback), so the 'Swiss with DE440s' leg was replaced by jplephem reading the kernel directly.

findings.title: Truncated VSOP87 series, not the reduction, sets the engine's accuracy floor (up to 15.6" today)
findings.claim: astronomy-engine 2.1.19 evaluates a VSOP87 cut down to 12-58 longitude terms per planet (Mercury L=12, Venus 13, Earth 32, Mars 58, Jupiter 41, Saturn 49, Uranus 45, Neptune 13; smallest longitude amplitude kept: Neptune 18.6", Mercury 15.6", Venus 2.5", Jupiter/Uranus 2.0", Saturn 1.8", Mars 0.5", Earth 0.3"). The resulting geocentric direction error, measured geometric-to-geometric against DE440s with no reduction or Delta-T involved, is Neptune p50 15.0"/max 15.6", Saturn 8.0"/9.1", Uranus 4.2"/5.0", Jupiter 2.6"/4.0", Venus 2.1"/7.1", Mercury 2.2"/5.4", Mars 1.1"/4.9", Sun 0.7"/1.7", Moon 1.3"/4.4", Pluto 1.4"/1.5" (daily 2025). The full shipped chain with TT pinned gives the same numbers (Neptune lon +11.6" mean with lat +9.6", Saturn -7.8", Uranus -1.4" with lat +4.1", Jupiter -2.0"), so light-time/aberration/precession/nutation contribute under ~0.3" and the series is the whole gap to Swiss. Swiss's .se1 (DE431) agrees with DE440s to 0.000-0.003" on the same rows.
findings.evidence: <worktree>/node_modules/astronomy-engine/astronomy.js:386 (const vsop) and :2918-2979 (VsopFormula/CalcVsop); term counts in <audit>/production-positions/vsop-term-counts.txt; residuals in compare.json keys T2_daily2025_pinnedTT_engine_minus_swissApparent and T8b_daily2025_geometric_series_only; arbiter horizons/arbiter.json: at 2025-07-01 00:00 TT engine-Horizons Saturn -8.334" lon/-1.77" lat, Neptune +11.501"/+9.632", Uranus -1.306"/+3.987", while Swiss-Horizons is +0.046..0.048" for every body. The committed in-suite gate (docs/engine-validation/README.md: Saturn 1.93" at 2020-01-01) misses this because the truncation error is long-period and two dates cannot see it.
findings.reproduction: cd <scratch>/audit/production-positions && node instants.mjs && node engine-dump.mjs && <swisslab>/venv/bin/python swiss-dump.py instants.json swiss.json && ./jplvenv/bin/python de440-dump.py instants.json de440.json && node compare.mjs  (total < 10 s); Horizons queries recorded in horizons/*.txt.query (QUANTITIES=31, CENTER=500@399, TIME_TYPE=TT, APPARENT=AIRLESS).
findings.impact: Every planet except the Sun/Mars is 2-16" from Swiss and from Horizons in ordinary modern charts, a hundred times the 0.13" the DE440s prototype already achieves; this alone keeps the stack below Swiss and no reduction work can fix it.
findings.fix: Replace astronomy-engine's planetary/Moon series with a DE440s (or DE441 for 1550-2650) Chebyshev pack compiled by examples/precision-alpha/tools/compiler (the committed prototype reached 0.134" max vs Swiss on 160 rows) and keep astronomy-engine only as a fallback outside pack coverage, flagged. If a data download is unacceptable for the homepage bundle, ship full VSOP87 (Sun/planets, ~0.1-1") plus ELP2000-82B (Moon) as a lazy chunk and reserve the DE pack for the full chart; either way stop shipping the 1-arcminute truncation.

findings.title: Delta-T model is 6.7 s too large today (>=5.4 s beyond any physical value), 110 s at 2100, and is neither exposed nor documented
findings.claim: astronomy-engine's DeltaT_EspenakMeeus (2005-2050 polynomial 62.92+0.32217u+0.005589u^2) gives 75.50 s at 2026-09-22 while Swiss gives 68.82 s. Independently of Swiss, TT-UTC is exactly 69.184 s in 2026 and |UT1-UTC| < 0.9 s, so the true Delta-T lies in [68.3, 70.1] s and the engine is at least 5.4 s high. Measured Moon displacement on the production UT path: 3.41" at modern-06 (2026-09-20T08Z) vs 0.10" with TT pinned. Ladder 1800-2200 (engine minus Swiss): -5.1 s (1800, Moon -3.0"), -0.05..+0.7 s 1940-2010, +2.5 s 2020, +8.5 s 2030 (4.3"), +19.2 s 2050 (10.4"), +36.8 s 2060 (slope kink at the 2050 branch), +110.4 s 2100 (54.4"), +207 s 2150 (114"), +280 s 2200 (173"), +537 s 2400 (Moon 303"). The package has no Delta-T API, receipt field or README statement (grep of dist/*.js, *.d.ts, README.md finds none); the receipt conventions block omits the time scale entirely.
findings.evidence: astronomy.js:1023-1136 (DeltaT_EspenakMeeus), :1157 (TerrestrialTime), chunk-GBH7JIYF.js MakeTime(date) calls; compare.json key T9_deltaT_ladder (columns engine_deltaT_s, swiss_deltaT_s, moon_displacement_arcsec, measured_moon_lon_diff_productionUT_arcsec agree to <1"); command output 'DELTA-T TODAY' in this session (AE 75.50 s / Swiss 68.82 s at 2026-09-22); committed docs/platform/evidence/swiss-benchmark/RESULTS.md already concedes the 2100 figure (this adds the present-day error and the 1800-2200 ladder).
findings.reproduction: node -e "const A=require('astronomy-engine');const t=A.MakeTime(new Date('2026-09-22T00:00:00Z'));console.log((t.tt-t.ut)*86400)" -> 75.50; python: swe.deltat_ex(swe.julday(2026,9,22,0), swe.FLG_SWIEPH)*86400 -> 68.82; node compare.mjs (T9).
findings.impact: The Moon of every chart cast today is displaced ~3.5" by the time scale alone, growing ~0.6"/yr, and any far-future or far-past chart is dominated by this; Swiss uses an IERS-tabulated Delta-T with a documented extrapolation and exposes swe_deltat/swe_set_delta_t_userdef.
findings.fix: Add a Delta-T module: IERS/Bulletin-A tabulated values through the present, Stephenson-Morrison-Hohenkerk 2016 spline for the past, a documented extrapolation beyond the table, an override input (pin Delta-T or pass TT directly), and a receipt field recording the value used. Inject it via astronomy-engine's SetDeltaTFunction until the series are replaced.

findings.title: computeChart passes the MEAN obliquity to the angles while bodies use the TRUE ecliptic and GAST: Ascendant off by up to 18.5" vs Swiss today
findings.claim: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js computeChart builds angleInput with obliquity: meanObliquity(centuriesSinceJ2000(input.utc)) but gastHours: SiderealTime(...) (apparent, includes the equation of the equinoxes) and the bodies come from Rotation_EQJ_ECT (true ecliptic of date). Nutation in obliquity is +8.3" in 2025-2026 (Swiss ECL_NUT deps = 8.26" at 2026-09-20). Measured against swe.houses_ex on 28 cases (4 places x 7 instants in 2025-2026): Ascendant differences up to -18.51" (London 2026-09-20T20Z), 13.15" (Longyearbyen), 10.52" (New York), -11.25" (London 2025-07-01T00Z); MC differences +-1.9". Analytic sensitivity for an 8.26" obliquity error: max 1.8" at the equator, 10.4" at 40 deg, 18.4" at 51.5 deg, 39.9" at 60 deg. The receipt records this as the convention 'angles: gast-and-mean-obliquity', so it is documented but frame-inconsistent with its own body positions.
findings.evidence: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js (function computeChart, lines 'obliquity: meanObliquity(centuriesSinceJ2000(input.utc))' and 'gastHours: SiderealTime(MakeTime(input.utc))'); chunk-H7RJKCBO.js:9-13 (meanObliquity); receipt.js:143; artifacts asc-check.json, asc-engine.json, asc-obliquity-sensitivity.txt. The committed swiss-node-polar pack's 1.57" worst angle (docs/engine-validation/README.md) is six instants and does not bound this.
findings.reproduction: cd <scratch>/audit/production-positions && node asc-check.mjs (natalChart(...).angles.asc vs swe.houses_ex(jd, lat, lon, b'W', 0)[1][0]).
findings.impact: The Ascendant is the most time-sensitive chart element (1 minute of clock ~ 15' of arc); a 10-20" frame error is small astrologically but is an outright inconsistency Swiss does not have, and it invalidates any 'angles agree to 1.6"' claim outside the six frozen cases.
findings.fix: Use the true obliquity of date (astronomy-engine e_tilt(time).tobl, or the new nutation module) for the angles, compute T from TT not UTC, change the receipt convention string to 'gast-and-true-obliquity', regenerate the frozen angle fixtures and re-run the polar pack; one-line engine change plus fixtures.

findings.title: True node carries a -7.25" mean bias (p50 7.0", max 19.9" vs Swiss TRUE_NODE) caused by the analytic Moon's velocity, not by a definition difference; committed 6.07" maximum understates it
findings.claim: Daily 2025 with TT pinned, engine North Node minus Swiss TRUE_NODE: mean -7.25", p50 7.03", p95 12.65", max 19.90" (production UT path identical to 0.02"). The engine's construction (ascending node of the geocentric angular-momentum plane r x v of GeoMoonState, rotated to the true ecliptic of date) IS Swiss's object: rebuilding that node from Swiss's own geometric Moon state in the equator/ecliptic of date reproduces Swiss TRUE_NODE to p50 1.01", max 2.96", mean -0.07" (the residual is Swiss's own three-position finite-difference method, NODE_CALC_INTV). Doing the same test in the J2000 frame gives 12"/34" because Swiss's J2000-flag node is the of-date node precessed as a point, a confound to avoid. Node speed differs from Swiss by p50 1.13"/day, max 9.29"/day, of which up to 8.9"/day is the +-6 h central difference on a fast-wobbling quantity. Node latitude reported as 0 is correct by definition (Swiss TRUE_NODE lat max 0 over 2025). Nutation correction changes nothing (max 20.03" after), so the bias is the Improved Lunar Ephemeris out-of-plane velocity error.
findings.evidence: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js trueNodeLongitude (angular momentum from GeoMoonState; astronomy.js:2884-2897 GeoMoonState central difference dt=1e-5 d); compare.json key T7_node_daily2025; node-definition-ofdate.json; node-definition.json (J2000 confound); docs/engine-validation/README.md quotes 0.001685457 deg (6.07") as the measured maximum from six cases.
findings.impact: The node is the worst-behaved of the twelve shipped points (a 20" error is three times the Moon's), and it is the first place a Swiss user will notice a difference (Swiss prints the node to the arcsecond).
findings.fix: Compute the node from a DE-based Moon state (position and analytic velocity from the Chebyshev derivative) in the true ecliptic of date; the exact r x v with an analytic velocity will beat Swiss's own three-position method (1-3" internal noise measured). Derive node speed analytically (d/dt of atan2 of the rotated h) instead of +-6 h differencing. Add MEAN_NODE (Swiss has it; the engine does not) from the standard mean-element polynomial.

findings.title: Moon route (EclipticGeoMoon) applies no light-time/aberration (net -0.70", constant) on top of a 1.3"-4.4" analytic-series error that reaches 7.5" at 1800 and 20" at 2400
findings.claim: Swiss apparent minus Swiss TRUEPOS for the Moon is -0.703" mean, p50 0.701", max 0.761" over 2025 (the individually large legs are light-time with barycentric velocity, up to 21.6", and aberration, up to 20.9", which nearly cancel). The engine's Moon has neither: engine minus Swiss TRUEPOS (geometric) is -1.24" mean, p50 1.25", max 4.38"; engine minus Swiss apparent is -0.54" mean, p50 0.68", max 3.63" (2025, TT pinned) - so today the series bias and the missing correction partially cancel. Geometric vs DE440s: p50 1.31", max 4.43"; latitude max 1.14". Far epochs (TT pinned, lon): 1800 +7.55", 1850 +6.73", 1900 +2.92", 2100 +0.86" (Horizons: +0.68"), 2200 +3.28", 2400 +20.31". Horizons 2025-07-01 confirms -0.72" lon / -0.62" lat.
findings.evidence: astronomy.js:2840-2870 (EclipticGeoMoon: CalcMoon -> mean obliquity -> nutation -> true obliquity, no GeoVector/light-time), chunk-GBH7JIYF.js moonOfDate; compare.json keys T3_moon_daily2025_pinnedTT, T8_epochs (Moon rows), T8b (Moon); horizons/arbiter.json rows moon-2025-07-01 and moon-2100-01-01; examples/precision-alpha/CHART-ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md already notes the missing pass (this adds the 0.70" size and the series bias).
findings.impact: The Moon is the fastest body and the one users check against ephemeris tables; Swiss delivers it to ~0.05" of Horizons, the engine to 0.7-4" today and 7" in the 19th century.
findings.fix: DE440s Moon (EMB->Moon segment) reduced with the alpha's retarded-position and aberration modules (already validated against ERFA in examples/precision-alpha), with true-of-date rotation via the new nutation; keep EclipticGeoMoon only as the flagged fallback.

findings.title: Custom Pluto integrator drifts to -8" (2100), -29" (2200, Horizons-confirmed) and -33" (2400); +18.6" at 1800
findings.claim: astronomy-engine's Pluto (segmented gravity simulation from a state table, astronomy.js:3240-3340) is -1.36" mean (max 1.69") in 2025 but, TT pinned, +18.62" at 1800, +9.90" at 1850, +3.44" at 1900, -8.02" at 2100, -14.38" at 2150, -29.24" at 2200, -32.82" at 2400 versus Swiss; Horizons/DE441 at 2200-01-01 TT gives engine -29.74" lon / -7.77" lat while Swiss is -0.50" (DE431 vs DE441 Pluto).
findings.evidence: compare.json key T8_epochs (Pluto rows), T2 (Pluto), horizons/arbiter.json row pluto-bary-2200-01-01.
findings.impact: Pluto is inside the site's accepted 1800-2199 span at 18.6" and 29" error; Swiss is within 0.5" of DE441 there.
findings.fix: Take Pluto from the DE pack (DE440s barycentre; DE441 for the 1550-2650 span) and, to exceed Swiss, resolve the Pluto-system barycentre to the Pluto centre with plu060 (~0.1" effect Swiss does not apply).

findings.title: Nutation keeps 5 of the 77 IAU 2000B luni-solar terms: 0.2685" max longitude error (1900-2100), present in every shipped longitude
findings.claim: astronomy.js iau2000b evaluates only the five largest terms (Omega, 2(F-D+Omega), 2(F+Omega), 2Omega, l'). Against the published 77-term series (alpha's nut00b) over 73 050 daily TT instants 1900-2100: max |dpsi| error 0.2685" (JD 2452355.5), mean 0.061", max |deps| error 0.086". Against Swiss's nutation in 2025: p50 0.054", p95 0.167", max 0.216". The shipped chunk applies this via Rotation_EQJ_ECT (planets, node) and e_tilt/nutation (Moon), so the error enters every longitude 1:1; the alpha's replica nutAstronomyEngine matches the real astronomy-engine to 0 (verified). Residual-subtraction on shipped output is inconclusive because series errors dominate (p50 moves < 0.05"), so confirmation is by code path plus the measured dpsi gap.
findings.evidence: astronomy.js:1316-1353 (iau2000b), :1363 (e_tilt), :6638 (Rotation_EQJ_ECT), :2855 (EclipticGeoMoon nutation call); nutation-series.json; compare.json key T2_dpsi_swiss_minus_ae_arcsec_daily2025; committed docs/platform/evidence/precision-2026-09-20/README.md:35 (0.2677").
findings.impact: A 0.27" floor under every body and the angles; Swiss uses the full model. Becomes the dominant error once the series are replaced.
findings.fix: Use examples/precision-alpha/src/core/nutation.mjs (77-term 2000B, or 2000A for a further 0.0025") in the of-date rotation and in the true obliquity; if astronomy-engine stays, wrap its rotations rather than calling Rotation_EQJ_ECT.

findings.title: Gravitational light deflection absent: 1.14" measured at Jupiter's 2025 conjunction; receipt's 'apparent' label is therefore not the IAU apparent place
findings.claim: Swiss apparent minus Swiss NOGDEFL over 3285 body-days in 2025: max -1.140" (Jupiter 2025-06-25, elongation 0.26 deg), +0.758" (Jupiter 06-24), 0.467" (Uranus 05-17, 0.89 deg); 116 body-days (3.5%) >= 0.05", 35 >= 0.1", 2 >= 0.5". The engine tracks the NOGDEFL variant (Jupiter residual stays at its -1.5..-1.7" series bias vs NOGDEFL while swinging -0.48..-2.31" vs apparent), confirming absence rather than assuming it. Swiss's speed includes the deflection derivative near conjunction (up to 8.57"/day for Uranus 2025-05-18, 1.83"/day Jupiter), which the engine lacks. The receipt declares planetPositions 'apparent-geocentric-ecliptic-of-date' although deflection is missing and nutation truncated. Committed CHART-ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md:19 states 32.87% of days 1900-2100 have a body inside the 5-degree floor.
findings.evidence: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js eclipticOfDate (GeoVector(body,time,true) only); receipt.js:140; compare.json key T4_deflection_daily2025 and T5 Jupiter/Uranus max rows.
findings.impact: Up to 1.7" at the solar limb, ~0.1-1" for a few days around every superior conjunction; Swiss applies it by default.
findings.fix: Port examples/precision-alpha/src/core/deflection.mjs (validated against ERFA) into the planet chain; reword the receipt to enumerate the corrections actually applied.

findings.title: +-6 h central-difference speed is off by up to 7.5"/day for the Moon; station times differ from Swiss by up to 38 min but the derivative contributes at most 1.1 min
findings.claim: Daily 2025, TT pinned: shipped speed minus Swiss FLG_SPEED for the Moon p50 1.80"/day, p95 5.33"/day, max 8.72"/day, of which the pure discretisation error (shipped minus h=0.001 d derivative of the same longitude) is p50 1.79, p95 5.25, max 7.47"/day; Mercury discretisation up to 1.70"/day near perihelion; outer planets < 0.005"/day. Retrograde flag: 0 disagreements with Swiss in 3650 body-days. Over the 54 stations of Mercury..Pluto in 2024-2026 (Swiss speed=0 bisected to 1e-6 d), the shipped station time differs from Swiss by median 0.06 h and max 0.63 h (Pluto 2024-10-12), 0.44 h Neptune, 0.26 h Uranus, <= 0.11 h Mercury/Venus, and the shipped minus tight-derivative station difference is <= 0.018 h; so a wrong retrograde flag is confined to a <= 38 min window whose width is set by the series error, not the derivative. Only longitude speed is produced (no latitude or distance rate; Swiss gives all three).
findings.evidence: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js longitudeSpeed (stepDays = 0.25); compare.json keys T5_speed_daily2025_pinnedTT, T5b_retrograde_flag_disagreements_daily2025; stations.json, stations-swiss.json.
findings.reproduction: node compare.mjs; <swisslab>/venv/bin/python stations-swiss.py && node stations-engine.mjs (about 20 s).
findings.impact: Small today; it becomes the limiting error for the Moon's speed once positions reach 0.1", and speed-dependent products (void-of-course, applying/separating, station lists) inherit it.
findings.fix: Derive velocities analytically from the Chebyshev state (position and derivative) through the reduction (the alpha already carries derivative enclosures), and emit lon, lat and distance rates; until then shrink the step to ~0.02 d, which removes the Moon error at negligible cost.

findings.title: No validity span or out-of-range flag: the package computes any year and silently degrades (Moon 303" and Pluto 33" at 2400)
findings.claim: computeBodies accepts any Date; astronomy-engine's Pluto table spans years 0-4000 and crawls beyond, VSOP87 and the ILE Moon are evaluated without limit. Measured production residuals vs Swiss at 2399-12-01: Moon 302.6" (20.3" with TT pinned), Pluto -33.2", Venus 26.8", Sun 22.0"; at 1800-02-01: Moon 5.0"/7.6" pinned, Neptune -16.1", Pluto 18.6". No flag is raised and the receipt COVERAGE says only 'finite-reference-cases-only'; the 1800-2199 limit is a site rule. Swiss returns an error or a flagged Moshier fallback outside its file span.
findings.evidence: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js computeBodies/computeChart (flags only 'polar-fallback'/'no-time'); receipt.js:148; compare.json key T8_epochs rows epoch-1800, epoch-2200, epoch-2400.
findings.impact: Callers of the public npm package cannot tell a 0.5" chart from a 300" one; Swiss can.
findings.fix: Declare a validity span per source (pack coverage, fallback series) in the receipt, add a flag such as 'outside-reference-span' and, for the DE pack, refuse or fall back explicitly outside coverage.

findings.title: DE431 (Swiss .se1) vs DE440s is 0.003" or less: moving to DE440/441 gains nothing against Swiss by itself; the premise that Swiss can read de440s.bsp is false
findings.claim: Swiss geometric ICRS positions from sepl_18/semo_18 (DE431 excerpts) versus jplephem on de440s.bsp, daily 2025: all ten bodies max 0.000-0.003" angular separation; at the 1900/2000/2100 epochs 0.000-0.006" (Moon 2100 largest). Horizons (DE441) vs Swiss in 2025: +0.046..0.048" (a constant that is the practical ceiling of 'agreement with Swiss'); Pluto 2200: Swiss -0.50" vs DE441. Attempting swe.set_jpl_file('de440s.bsp') with FLG_JPLEPH returned retflag 260 (FLG_MOSEPH set, FLG_JPLEPH clear): Swiss 2.10.03 does not read NAIF SPK files and silently fell back to Moshier, so the 'Swiss with DE440s' leg requested by the task does not exist on this machine and was replaced by reading the kernel directly. Saturn centre vs system barycentre (Horizons 699 vs 6) differs by 0.024" lon / 0.010" lat; Swiss reports barycentres.
findings.evidence: compare.json keys T8b_daily2025_geometric_series_only (swissICRS_geom_vs_DE440s_sep), T8_epochs (geom_swissICRS_vs_DE440s_sep), T8c (frame bias 0.022"); swiss-jpl-probe.txt; horizons/arbiter.json.
findings.impact: Sets expectations: the path to exceeding Swiss is series replacement plus a fuller reduction and independent arbitration (Horizons/DE441, SOFA/ERFA), not a newer DE alone; a claim of 'DE440 therefore better than Swiss' would be unsupported at the 0.01" level.
findings.fix: Frame the roadmap around (a) full-precision series, (b) complete IAU reduction, (c) planet centres via satellite kernels, (d) Horizons/DE441 arbitration; record in the evidence tree that Swiss cannot consume .bsp files.

findings.title: Frame-chain nits: FK5 obliquity 84381.448" in the VSOP rotation vs P03 84381.406" in precession, no ICRS frame bias (0.022"), heliocentric aberration velocity, UTC taken as UT1
findings.claim: VsopRotate (astronomy.js:2956) rotates VSOP87 ecliptic to the equator with cos/sin of the IAU 1976 obliquity while precession_rot (:1794) uses eps0 = 84381.406" (P03), a 0.042" internal inconsistency; the J2000/FK5 to ICRS frame bias is not applied (Swiss J2000 vs ICRS output differs by 0.0221" on every 2025 row); BodyPosition.Position (:3750-3780) uses the heliocentric, not barycentric, Earth velocity for aberration (<= 0.01"); MakeTime treats UTC as UT1 (|UT1-UTC| <= 0.9 s, <= 0.5" Moon) exactly as swe_calc_ut does, so no Swiss gap; centuriesSinceJ2000 for the mean obliquity uses UTC not TT (negligible). Rotation order (precession then nutation then obliquity), longitude atan2(y,x) and latitude asin(z/r) in eclipticOfDate are correct. None of these is measurable beneath the series error today; all become relevant at the 0.01" level.
findings.evidence: astronomy.js lines cited; compare.json key T8c_swiss_J2000_vs_ICRS_frame_bias_sep.
findings.impact: Sub-0.05" today; needed to exceed Swiss (which applies frame bias and full reduction) once the series are fixed.
findings.fix: When adopting the DE pack, start from ICRS, apply the IAU 2006/2000A bias-precession-nutation matrix (the alpha's frames.mjs already does), use the barycentric observer velocity, and accept UT1-UTC from an optional input.

findings.title: Capability gaps versus Swiss in the body set and outputs
findings.claim: The package returns lon/lat/lon-speed for Sun, Moon, eight planets and the true nodes only. Absent relative to swe_calc: geocentric distance, latitude and distance rates, mean node, mean and osculating apogee (Lilith), Chiron and asteroids, Earth/heliocentric and barycentric frames, topocentric positions (FLG_TOPOCTR; parallax moves the Moon up to ~1 deg), sidereal zodiac/ayanamsas, equatorial output, J2000/mean-of-date outputs, Delta-T access, and planet-centre vs system-barycentre handling. Unconfirmed: whether any site surface needs these today; the site wrappers are another auditor's area.
findings.evidence: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js PLANETS list and position() return shape; index.d.ts public API (natalChart/transits/synastry/saturnReturn/moonPhase/findLongitudeCrossings).
findings.impact: Users migrating from Swiss expect these; some (distance, topocentric Moon) are prerequisites for features such as parallax-corrected charts that would exceed Swiss's default geocentric output.
findings.fix: Extend the body/position model to carry distance and full state, add mean node and mean apogee from standard mean elements, add topocentric and sidereal modes as options with receipt fields; asteroids/Chiron need additional SPK segments.
